title: Tumour-on-a-Chip Model
imageAlt: Fluorescence microscopy of the tumour-on-a-chip model
summary: Fabricating microfluidic devices and studying cells to model the tumour microenvironment in vitro.
overview: As a Research Assistant at the Integrative Biology and Microengineered Technologies (IBMT) Laboratory, I contributed to a tumour-on-a-chip platform under the mentorship of PhD student Han Shao and Professor Edmond Young. The platform models the tumour microenvironment in vitro.

sections.title: Device fabrication & cell culture
paragraphs: My work included microfluidic channel design, PDMS casting, and device bonding.
I used sterile techniques to culture MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells, GFP-A549 lung cancer cells, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells.

sections.title: Imaging & analysis
paragraphs: I worked with brightfield and fluorescence microscopy and performed quantitative analysis of cell morphology and growth. The project explores a platform for studying tumour progression, cancer–stroma interactions, and therapeutic response.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Production Planning
imageAlt: VPDP: Specformer encoder and CORAL ordinal head for integer production predictions

gallery.imageAlt: VPDP: vulcanization autoclave scheduling and star capacity for different hose types

summary: Exploring graph neural networks for vulcanizing planning decisions in rubber manufacturing.
overview: This project explored graph neural networks (GNNs) for the Vulcanizing Planning Decision Problem in rubber manufacturing, representing the relationships between jobs, machines, and production constraints.

sections.title: Graph representation
paragraphs: The model used message passing across machine–job graphs to represent scheduling dependencies and variable–constraint relationships, incorporating demand and resource constraints.

sections.title: Model development
paragraphs: Work focused on developing and tuning the GNN architecture and evaluating the balance between scalability and predictive accuracy on large problem instances.

title: Fashion Image Classification
summary: Comparing three neural network architectures for clothing image classification with PyTorch.
overview: I built an image classification project in PyTorch using Fashion-MNIST, a dataset of 70,000 clothing images spanning categories such as shoes, dresses, and pants.

sections.title: Architecture comparison
paragraphs: I implemented three neural network architectures and compared their image recognition accuracy. TinyVGG achieved the highest accuracy among the models evaluated in this project.

title: Hot Dog Detection with Faster R-CNN
imageAlt: Faster R-CNN hot dog detection project
summary: Training a Faster R-CNN model to locate hot dogs in images using a custom annotated dataset.
overview: I developed a computer vision model in PyTorch using the Faster R-CNN architecture to detect hot dogs in images.

sections.title: Dataset & training
paragraphs: The model was trained on a custom dataset in COCO format with annotations recording the positions of hot dogs. I evaluated its detection performance using precision metrics.

title: Machined Piston & Slider Crank
imageAlt: Machined piston and slider-crank course project
summary: Turning machining practice into a working piston and slider-crank mechanism powered by compressed air.
overview: I took a basic machining course at George Brown College to develop practical experience with manufacturing tools and techniques.

sections.title: From tools to mechanism
paragraphs: The course introduced the mill, drill press, and lathe. I applied these techniques to machine a single piston with a functional slider-crank mechanism.
The piston operates by feeding compressed air into the block.

title: Urban Concept Steering Wheel
summary: Creating the steering wheel CAD model for the team's 2023 Urban Concept car.
overview: As a member of the University of Toronto Supermileage design team, I created the steering wheel CAD model for the 2023 Urban Concept car.

sections.title: CAD work
paragraphs: I used SolidWorks to model the steering wheel as part of the team's vehicle design work.

overview: This portfolio uses custom HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to bring my engineering, research, and machine learning projects together in one place.

sections.title: Exploring the work
